accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:known-cell-score-laws
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Within-cell score laws are maintained outcome-independent inputs, not estimated by the proposed procedure.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: All sharp-set, dual, approximation, and confidence claims are conditional on the supplied within-cell score laws.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:surface-lipschitz
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The arm-specific Lipschitz radii are maintained sensitivity parameters selected outside boundary-RD theory.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: All endpoint and sign claims are conditional on each reported pair (M_0,M_1), with substantive conclusions limited to the prespecified sensitivity grid.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 4–6, equations (2.1)–(2.4) and concluding discussion at lines 310–315
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Equation (2.1) is Euclidean Lipschitz smoothness, equation (2.2) is the bounded isotropic optimization, equation (2.3) is the one-coordinate weakening, and the paper calls development of the tight (2.2) bounds an open interest.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1304.7014v3 corroborating the cited 2016 ARMA article
source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 2, displayed flat-metric variational formula; p. 7, Theorem 13
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 13 identifies generalized W_1^{1,1} with the flat metric; the displayed variational form is an unequal-mass partial-transport expression without areal side moments.
Theorem 1 gives a pre-aggregation convergence/MSE result and Theorem 2 gives asymptotic normality and usual large-sample confidence intervals for a unit-level boundary aggregation estimator.
The paper uses individual bivariate-score observations and provides pointwise and uniform confidence intervals/bands for the boundary treatment-effect curve.
The paper develops a moment/SoS hierarchy for transport, proves convergence as order increases, and describes approximation of linear quantities and transport-map support from moments.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv preprint corresponding to Journal of Symbolic Computation 128 (2025) 102403
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies exact moment representation and flat truncation, with flat truncation tied to zero-dimensional support of the minimizer quadratic module.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a short explicit separation result showing a polygonal fixed-areal instance where the Qiu–Stoye one-coordinate outer bound is strictly wider than the exact clipped areal interval; this would make the informed-by comparison operational rather than solely contextual.
Promote the verified-reconstruction question into a constructive theorem target by specifying an input-size model and a termination/bit-complexity bound for the rational certificate routine.

Add a worked non-rectangular empirical-design example showing how changing a plausible within-cell score law changes the sign certificate, thereby stress-testing the maintained-law sensitivity protocol.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with the conditional maintained-input scope fixed; preserve the open verified-reconstruction problem as a separate constructive target.
